manuscript_passages.quote: Contributors scored higher than lurkers in the reported post hoc comparison
their lower reported self-efficacy than contributors warrants attention

source_locations: new-evidence.md, PDF p. 7, survey instrument and attention-check exclusions
new-evidence.md, PDF pp. 9–10, Table 2 and ANOVA/Tukey results
source_evidence: 272 survey completers and removal of 22 attention-check failures are reported, yet subsequent group Ns total 272.
Three-group ANOVA statistics are printed as F(271), without the requisite two degrees of freedom.
Contributors' self-efficacy N=110 and SD=9.96 imply a conventional 95% mean interval half-width near 1.88; the printed 44.09–46.82 interval has a half-width near 1.37.
shared_verification_findings.why_it_matters: The comparatively small self-efficacy result underlies both passages' interpretation. Internal statistical reporting should agree before the inference is independently certified.
shared_verification_findings.action: Verify sample flow, original table values/layout, ANOVA degrees of freedom and Tukey output against authorized original-source or analysis records. Do not invent corrected statistics.
shared_verification_findings.manuscript_consequence: No demonstrated mandatory correction: both manuscripts accurately describe the reported comparison and do not reproduce the inconsistent numerical details.
shared_verification_findings.limits: Extraction may disturb tables; raw data and analysis output are unavailable; these discrepancies do not establish that the reported group difference is false.
